key_insight: Usable GHZ-state size can fall far below processor qubit count: the best superconducting devices passed at 27 and 24 qubits, while a 12-qubit trapped-ion device passed with its full register.
engineering_relevance: Application-specific cloud benchmarks can guide hardware selection more reliably than physical qubit counts or median calibration metrics alone.
method: Benchmarked nine cloud-accessible processors from five vendors across superconducting and trapped-ion technologies.
Used QuSquare multipartite entanglement tests and direct fidelity estimation with default compilation and no error mitigation.
Searched for the largest GHZ state whose fidelity was statistically compatible with the F = 1/2 entanglement threshold.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that tightening the criterion from threshold compatibility to certified genuine multipartite entanglement reduced devices succeeding at any tested size from nine to four.
watch_item: Threshold compatibility does not certify entanglement, and reported passing sizes depend strongly on the statistical decision rule.
paper_title: Cross-Platform Benchmarking of GHZ-State Generation in Quantum Processors via Cloud Services
